Login sequence (Telnet, port 23/2324 via NAT):

Welcome to EPON.


User Access Verification

Username: admin
Password: admin

Epon>

Unprivileged prompt is "Epon> ". "help" is NOT a valid command ("% Unknown command: help") -- the discovery command is "?".

Epon>?
  enable  Turn on privileged mode command
  exit    Exit current mode and down to previous mode
  list    Print command list
  ping    ping functions
  show    Show running system information

NOTE ON SYNTAX ORDER: the "list" command (full grammar reference, see below)
places the optional vendor-keyword in parentheses FIRST and the INTERFACE
placeholder in the position it actually occupies on the command line -- do
not assume INTERFACE always comes last. Examples actually verified working
on this unit:
  show epon sfp-info 1/1          (keyword "sfp-info" BEFORE the interface)
  show epon 1/1 optical-ddm       (interface BEFORE the keyword "optical-ddm")
  show onu optical-ddm epon 1/1 1 (onu optical-ddm epon <IF> <onu-id>)
  show onu config epon 1/1 1      (onu config epon <IF> <onu-id>)
  show pon 1 statistic            (bare port number, no "epon" keyword, no slash)
  show nni 1 statistic            (bare port number, same pattern)
A command guessed by "probably symmetric" ordering was tried and rejected
by the device ("show epon 1/1 sfp-info" -> "% Unknown command"). Always
verify the exact token order against the "list" output or a live "?"
before using a new show/config command in the driver.

NOTE: entering this per-EPON-port config context (interface epon <X/Y>) does
NOT by itself change the running-config -- it only moves the CLI prompt one
level deeper, exactly like Cisco IOS "interface" sub-mode. No write/commit
happens until a config-changing command is actually typed inside it.

--- ONU authorization grammar (this is the mechanism that gates
    discoverUnconfiguredOnus / authorizeOnu / blockOnu / unblockOnu) ---

Epon(config-epon1/1)#auth mode ?
  disable  -- Disable auth function
  hybrid   -- Hybrid auth mode
  loid     -- Loid based auth mode
  mac      -- Mac based auth mode

Epon(config-epon1/1)#whitelist ?
  add     -- Add whitelist entry
  clear   -- Clear whitelist table
  delete  -- Delete whitelist entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#whitelist add ?
  MACADDR  -- Mac address.example: 78:5c:72:00:11:22

Epon(config-epon1/1)#blacklist ?
  add     -- Add blacklist entry
  clear   -- Clear blacklist table
  delete  -- Delete blacklist entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#loidlist ?
  add     -- Add loid entry
  clear   -- Clear loid table
  delete  -- Delete loid entry

Epon(config-epon1/1)#loidlist add ?
  LOID  -- Loid value, 6-24 character

Epon(config-epon1/1)#add ?
  onu  -- Onu config

Epon(config-epon1/1)#add onu ?
  <1-128>  -- Specified Onu Id

UNVERIFIED: whether "add onu <id>" takes any further argument (e.g. a MAC to
bind to that slot) after the id, or is a complete command as-is. The device
only ever showed "<1-128> -- Specified Onu Id" as the sole completion at
this depth; the next token was never probed because doing so would be the
first state-changing command on this port (no physical ONU exists yet to
safely validate against). DO NOT implement authorizeOnu's "add onu" step
without probing "add onu 1 ?" first, ideally once a real ONU is physically
present so the end-to-end effect can be observed.

CONFIRMED real syntax in actual use on this unit (captured verbatim from
"show running-config", not guessed):
  onu 1 vlan port 1 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 2 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 3 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
  onu 1 vlan port 4 vlan-mode tag pvid 400
(one line per physical LAN port on the ONU, port numbers 1-4 observed)

--- quirks that any driver/parser MUST account for ---

1. PAGER: some "show" outputs longer than one screen stop with the literal
   line "--- Enter Key To Continue ----" and wait for an Enter keypress
   before continuing (see show_onu_config_paginated.txt). A driver's telnet
   client must detect this marker and send a bare newline to page through,
   or it will hang forever waiting for the real prompt.

2. STREAMING/BLOCKING COMMAND -- AVOID: "show epon <IF> counter-change"
   never returned to the "Epon# " prompt during reconnaissance and appears
   to be a live/continuously-refreshing view (like a "watch"), not a
   one-shot report. Sending it from an automated session with no way to
   send Ctrl+C left the whole telnet session stuck (every subsequent
   command sent in that same session was silently swallowed, interpreted
   as keystrokes inside the live view instead of as new CLI commands).
   Do not use this command in the driver without first confirming the
   correct way to exit it (Ctrl+C was not tested).

3. INTERFACE NAMING IS NOT CONSISTENT ACROSS CONTEXTS for the same physical
   EPON port 1 on slot 1:
     - "show interfaces status"      -> "Epon 1/1"   (capitalized, space)
     - "show vlan" (port membership) -> "Pon1/1"     (no space, "Pon" not "Epon")
     - CLI command argument syntax   -> "epon 1/1"   (lowercase keyword + space + slot/port)
     - "show interfaces brief"       -> does not list EPON ports at all,
       only the GE1/1-4 copper uplinks.
   A driver's parser must not assume one canonical interface-name string
   works across all show commands; each command's own format must be
   parsed on its own terms.

4. "show olt mac" / "show olt mac epon 1/1" only ever showed the table
   header ("ID    mac               valid static_flag aging port_id") with
   zero data rows, because no ONU is physically connected yet. The actual
   column data format for a populated row is UNVERIFIED -- do not write a
   row-parsing regex until a real populated table has been captured.

5. OLT-side optical DDM ("show epon <IF> optical-ddm") only exposes
   Temperature / Voltage / TxBias / TxPower -- there is no RxPower field on
   the OLT's own EPON port, unlike a GPON OLT. This is architecturally
   expected: EPON upstream reception is burst-mode per-ONU, so a
   continuous "RxPower" reading for the whole PON port does not apply the
   same way it would on a GPON card.

   UPDATE (real ONU connected 2026-10-08): per-ONU optical DDM DOES include
   RxPower once the ONU is actually online -- "show onu optical-ddm epon
   <IF> <onu-id>" for an online ONU returns 5 fields in this order:
   Temperature, Voltage, TxBias, TxPower, RxPower (see
   show_onu_optical-ddm_online.txt). Two distinct error strings exist for
   the not-online case, not just one:
     "! Onu <id> is offline!"  -> that onu-id has a known/provisioned
                                   binding but is not currently registered.
     "! Onu <id> invalid"      -> that onu-id has never been seen/bound on
                                   that port at all (no MAC ever learned).
   Do not treat these as the same state in a parser -- "invalid" vs
   "offline" are different pieces of information.

6. ONU-ID ASSIGNMENT IS MAC-BASED AND PERSISTENT, NOT A SIMPLE "FIRST FREE
   SLOT 1,2,3...". When a real ONU was connected to epon 1/1 for the first
   time, it was auto-assigned onu-id 2, NOT onu-id 1 (which had a leftover
   MAC binding -- e4:2d:7b:0f:3b:cf, status Down -- from some earlier
   test/registration, confirmed via "show onu upgrade-state epon 1/1").
   Never assume "the first ONU connected becomes onu-id 1" when writing
   discovery logic -- the real onu-id must always be read back from the
   device (e.g. from the port_id column of "show olt mac", formatted
   "onu_<slot>/<port>:<onu-id>"), never computed/guessed.

7. "show onu upgrade-state epon <IF>" is NOT just about firmware upgrades
   despite the name -- it is actually the richest real per-ONU status
   table found so far: OnuId, MacAddress, Status (Up/Down), ChipId, Ge/Fe/
   Pots (hardware port counts on the ONU itself), CtcStatus (PON
   registration/negotiation state, e.g. "CtcNegDone"), CtcVer, Uptime (the
   ONU's own uptime, not the OLT's), Firmware, UpgradeState. This is a
   better candidate than "show olt mac" for a future "list registered
   ONUs on this port" driver method, since it also reports online/offline
   status and firmware version per ONU (see show_onu_upgrade-state.txt).

8. A newly auto-registered ONU (recognized at the PON/MAC layer, appears
   in "show olt mac" and "show onu upgrade-state") has ZERO VLAN/service
   config by default -- "show onu config epon <IF> <new-onu-id>" returns
   just the bare "! Onu <slot>/<port>:<id> configuration" header with no
   "onu ... vlan port ..." lines (see show_onu_config_unprovisioned.txt).
   It will not pass real customer traffic until explicitly provisioned
   with the same "onu <id> vlan port <n> vlan-mode tag pvid <vlan>"
   command already confirmed in show_running-config.txt for onu-id 1.

9. "show olt mac" (no filter) and "show olt mac epon <IF>" (filtered) both
   work and return the same row shape; "show olt mac cache" also works and
   returns what looks like the same table (possibly a faster/precomputed
   read instead of a live poll — difference not fully characterized). The
   MAC address shown for a given onu_<slot>/<port>:<id> entry in "show olt
   mac" did NOT exactly match the MacAddress shown for the same onu-id in
   "show onu upgrade-state" in one real observation (04:B0:E7:D3:09:A8 vs
   04:b0:e7:d3:09:a6, differing in the last octet) -- do not assume these
   two commands' MAC columns are always interchangeable/the same value
   without further verification; they may represent different interfaces
   of the same ONU (e.g. management vs data MAC) or one table may simply
   be stale relative to the other.

10. "show version" / "show system" never required paging (one screen).
   "show running-config" / "show interfaces status" were multi-section
   but also fit without triggering the pager on this unit's current
   (nearly-empty) configuration; a production config with many VLANs/ONUs
   provisioned may trigger the pager on these too.

11. DANGEROUS QUIRK CONFIRMED THE HARD WAY: sending "<complete command> ?"
   as one line over a raw TCP/Telnet socket (no real terminal) does NOT
   behave like a Cisco terminal's inline help. The device echoes the help
   text (e.g. "<cr>") for the TYPED portion before the "?", but because a
   trailing CR/LF follows the "?" in the same line, it ALSO submits and
   EXECUTES the typed command for real once it is already a complete,
   valid command (e.g. "onu 2 activate ?" both showed help AND executed
   "onu 2 activate"). This only happens when the text before "?" is
   already complete on its own — an INCOMPLETE command (e.g. "onu 2 ?",
   "add onu 2 ?", "dereg ?") is safe: the device answers "% Incomplete
   command." and nothing is executed. CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-10-08: this
   accidentally deactivated the real connected ONU (onu-id 2) via
   "onu 2 deactivate ?", observed via "show onu upgrade-state" (Status
   flipped Down, CtcStatus MpcpDiscovery) before being manually reversed
   with a plain "onu 2 activate" (no trailing "?"). RULE: never append
   "?" to a command string that might already be complete when driving
   this CLI programmatically — only use it on a prefix already known (or
   suspected) to be incomplete, or split connection per probe so an
   accidental execution can't chain into the next command.

12. ONU pre-registration grammar completed live (resolves the "UNVERIFIED"
   note above about "add onu <id>"): the full command is
   "add onu <1-128> <MAC> <ONU-TYPE>" — three arguments, not one. Verified
   step by step via incomplete-command "?" probing (safe, since each
   prefix was genuinely incomplete until the last argument):
     add onu 5 ?                           -> ONU-MAC (format xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx)
     add onu 5 04:b0:e7:aa:bb:cc ?         -> ONU-TYPE (example given: "onu-01g")
   Executing "add onu 5 04:b0:e7:aa:bb:cc onu-01g" (confirmed complete,
   no further args) for real created a phantom (no physical hardware)
   registration: it appeared in "show onu upgrade-state epon 1/1" as
   "1/1:5  04:b0:e7:aa:bb:cc  Down  0  1  0  0  MpcpDiscovery  0  0H0M0S --"
   (ChipId/Ge/Fe/Pots all 0 or placeholder, unlike a real connected ONU)
   but did NOT appear in "show olt mac" (that table only shows MACs
   actually learned off the wire) nor in "show running-config" under
   "White list configuration" (so this binding is NOT part of the
   persisted/saved whitelist section — likely pure runtime state until
   an actual ONU with that MAC links up, or the entry is removed).
   "onu-01g" was accepted as a valid ONU-TYPE value on this firmware; no
   command was found that enumerates the full list of valid types, so
   other type strings remain unverified.

13. REMOVING AN "add onu" BINDING: contrary to what the config-mode "?"
   tree advertises, "dereg onu <id>" and "dereg <MAC>" BOTH FAILED when
   actually executed against the phantom binding from note 12 ("! De-
   register onu failed!" and " Failed" respectively) — "dereg" being
   listed in the grammar does not mean it works on this firmware/scenario.
   The command that actually worked: "delete onu <1-128>" (discovered via
   the config-epon sub-mode's top-level "delete ?" -> "onu -- Onu config"
   -> "delete onu ?" -> "<1-128>"). "delete onu 5" removed the phantom
   binding cleanly (confirmed gone from "show onu upgrade-state"
   afterwards), with zero error output. "clear onu <id>" also exists in
   the grammar (same "<1-128>" shape) but was not tested since "delete
   onu" already worked — do not assume "clear onu" is equivalent without
   verifying it separately.

15. UPLINK TRUNK CONFIGURATION CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-10-09 (tested against
   "ten-gigabitethernet 1/2", a real uplink port with no SFP installed and
   no traffic — chosen specifically to avoid touching the ports actually
   carrying the real ONU). Full working sequence, confirmed via
   "show running-config" before/after:
     configure terminal
     vlan database                              -> enters "Epon(config-vlan)#"
     vlan <id> name <name>
     exit                                        -> back to "Epon(config)#"
     interface <interfaceName>                   -> e.g. "ten-gigabitethernet 1/2"
     switchport mode trunk
     switchport allowed vlan add <id> tagged
     exit
     exit
     write
   This creates the VLAN in the global "vlan database" AND trunks it
   (tagged) on the given interface in one shot — same two-step shape
   (global VLAN + per-interface trunk) as ZteC320Driver's own
   configureVlanOnInterface(). Implemented in HiosoDriver.configureVlanOnInterface(),
   capability now true.

16. "shutdown"/"no shutdown" ON A PHYSICAL INTERFACE (not an ONU) CONFIRMED
   LIVE 2026-10-09, same test interface as note 15. Sequence:
     configure terminal
     interface <interfaceName>
     shutdown        (or "no shutdown" to reverse)
     exit
     exit
     write
   Confirmed via "show running-config": the literal word "shutdown" appears
   under the interface block when administratively down, and disappears
   after "no shutdown" — exactly what HiosoDriver.discoverInterfaces()'s own
   parser already looks for (`shutdownMentioned` regex). Implemented in
   HiosoDriver.setInterfaceAdminState(), capability now true. Test interface
   left clean (back to "no shutdown" state) at the end of this test.

   STILL UNVERIFIED: whether "add onu <id> <mac> <type>" behaves safely
   when run against an onu-id that is ALREADY live/auto-registered (e.g.
   re-asserting the real onu-id 2's own binding) — only tested against a
   previously-unused id (5) with no physical ONU behind it. Do not assume
   this is a safe no-op on an already-connected real ONU without testing
   it deliberately first.

14. BANDWIDTH COMMAND GRAMMAR (full, confirmed live 2026-10-09 against the
   real connected ONU, onu-id 2 — this OLT only has this one ONU plugged
   in, there is no spare unit to test against): seven positional arguments,
   discovered one "?" at a time (each prefix genuinely incomplete until the
   last argument, so safe per the rule in note 11):
     onu <1-128> bandwidth <FIR-up> <CIR-up> <PIR-up> <weight-up> <weight-down> <PIR-down> <PBS-down>
   Ranges as reported by the device itself:
     FIR-up:     0-960000     ("Upstream fir")
     CIR-up:     0-960000     ("Upstream cir")
     PIR-up:     512-1000000  ("Upstream pir")
     weight-up:  1-16         ("Upstream weight")
     weight-down:1-16         ("Downstream weight")
     PIR-down:   0-1000000    ("Downstream pir")
     PBS-down:   0-1000000    ("Downstream pbs")
   All three upstream values (FIR/CIR/PIR) are in kbps; EPON has no
   per-ONU absolute downstream rate control beyond PIR/PBS because
   downstream is a shared broadcast medium from the OLT — the up/down
   "weight" pair is a DBA scheduling priority (1-16) between ONUs sharing
   the same PON port, not a bandwidth value itself.

   DANGEROUS QUIRK HIT AGAIN (same class as note 11): the full 7-argument
   form IS a complete command by itself. Appending "?" after supplying all
   seven values ("onu 2 bandwidth 100000 100000 100000 8 8 100000 100000 ?")
   showed the "<cr>" hint AND executed the command for real — it actually
   capped the real connected ONU's upstream and downstream to 100 Mbps.
   The ONU stayed Up/CtcNegDone throughout (unlike the activate/deactivate
   incident, this did not bounce the PON link), but it is a live example of
   the same mistake: never append "?" to a prefix that might already be a
   complete, valid command when driving this CLI programmatically. Values
   below 7 full arguments ("... bandwidth 100000 ?", "... 100000 100000 ?",
   etc.) were all genuinely incomplete and safe to probe with "?".
